Youth Empowerment for Climate Action Platform (YECAP), är en ungdomsledd regional plattform med syfte att säkerställa att unga, särskilt unga från marginaliserade grupper i Asien och Oceanien är meningsfullt engagerade och delaktiga i miljö/klimat på regional, nationell och lokal nivå. YECAP består av följande aktörer UNDP, UNFCCC, UNICEF, British Council, YOUNGO, Movers och 2030 Youth Force. Insatsen ska genomföras gemensamt av dessa aktörer med UNDP som avtalspart till Ambassaden och huvudsaklig ansvarig genomförare.
YECAP har lämnat in ett förslag för att genomföra projektet "Scaling up the Youth Empowerment in Climate Action Platform in Asia and the Pacific".
YECAP´s övergripande mål är att: Stärkt klimatstyrning för en effektiv utveckling och genomförande av klimatpolitik som är genus/könsinkluderande för att skydda unga och särskilt de mest marginaliserade, samtidigt som deras förmåga till klimatengagemang ökar.
För att uppnå detta övergripande mål kommer YECAP att fokusera på att stärka kapaciteten och utbilda unga förändringsaktörer. Projektet syftar också till att öka medvetenheten bland beslutsfattare om att systematiskt inkludera unga i alla stadier av beslutsprocesser relaterade till miljö och klimatanpassning, samt att identifiera ingångar för unga förändringsaktörer att påverka beslutsfattare.

Youth Empowerment in Climate Action (YECAP) is a youth-led regional Platform, for young people in the Asia Pacific region to meaningfully engage in climate action. The platform is co-convened by UNDP Asia-Pacific regional office, UNFCCC Regional Collaboration Centre for Asia-Pacific and UNICEF East Asia and the Pacific and South Asia, British Council in collaboration with youth organisations/youth constituencies such as YOUNGO, Movers Programme and 2030 Youth Force. YECAP has submitted a proposal to implement the project "Scaling up the Youth Empowerment in Climate Action Platform in Asia and the Pacific". The project aims to contribute to the overall goal "Climate change governance is strengthened for the effective development and implementation of gender-inclusive climate policies to protect young people and especially the most marginalised, while also helping them to increase the scale of their climate actions". To achieve this overall goal, YECAP will focus on strengthening capacity and training young change agents (e.g., youth-led local and regional civil society organizations) and bringing young people together with decision-makers. The project also aims to raise awareness among decision-makers to systematically include and support young people in all stages of decision-making processes.

During the reporting period, YECAP has reached a significant number of youth and stakeholders, and made progress in advancing youth engagement, capacity building, and leadership in climate governance across the Asia Pacific region. Through strategic partnerships, regional forums, and targeted training programs, YECAP empowered young people particularly those from underrepresented groups to meaningfully participate in national and international climate processes. One notable outcome is how YECAP supported youth committee contributed to the amendment of local climate laws, demonstrating the tangible impact of youth led advocacy at the subnational level.
A few key examples of the results are below.
- Youth Engagement in NDC 3.0: YECAP co-facilitated two major regional forums with UNFCCC RCC Asia-Pacific, directly engaging 126 government representatives and creating platforms for youth to co-develop inclusive climate strategies. These efforts strengthened youth-government collaboration and positioned young people as key stakeholders in shaping ambitious and equitable NDCs.
- Capacity Building for Inclusive Climate Policy: Over 600 youth were trained through initiatives such as the Youth Climate Action Lab, Regional Youth Parliament, and Shakers Fellowship. YECAP exceeded its annual target by facilitating youth participation in 15 climate policy consultations, ensuring diverse youth voices were reflected in climate governance.
- Local Policy Influence: Youth-committees played a crucial role in reviewing and providing feedback on local climate policies, such as the Natural Resources Protection Act and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act. Their contributions led to the amendment of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act in Madi Municipality, with revisions currently underway in Tilottama Municipality in Nepal.
- Strengthening Youth-Led CSOs: YECAP trained 42 CSO representatives and supported 30 organizations in designing gender-inclusive interventions. Through partnerships like the one with ARROW, youth contributed to global policy dialogues, including the Summit of the Future.
- Youth Entrepreneurship for Climate Solutions: Through the Springboard Climate Programme and the Youth Agri-Innovation Challenge, over 280 youth entrepreneurs were equipped with skills to develop climate-smart, gender-inclusive solutions, particularly in vulnerable regions like the Hindu Kush Himalaya.
- Indigenous Youth Representation: YECAP supported two Indigenous youth leaders from Nepal and Bangladesh to participate in LCIPP events at COP29 in Baku. They also joined the Youth Climate Action Lab to prepare for their engagement, highlighting the importance of Indigenous knowledge in climate adaptation.
- Youth Participation in Climate Forums: Over 3,300 youth from 35 countries engaged in national, regional, and global forums (e.g., APYDF, CED8, LCOYs, RCOY-APAC). Youth contributed to policy discussions, delivered statements, and connected with UN and government officials, strengthening their role in climate diplomacy and governance.
- Local Conferences of Youth (LCOYs): LCOYs in 11 countries enabled youth to co-develop National Youth Statements, influencing national climate policies and COP29 advocacy. Supported by 100 partners, LCOYs expanded access to rural and marginalized youth, ensuring inclusive participation beyond capital cities.
